title: Protocol for drug screening of patient-derived tumor organoids using high-content fluorescent imaging
protocol: Thaw Matrigel on ice at 4°C.
Prepare 9 mL of Advanced DMEM/F12 in one low-binding 15-mL tube and keep it on ice.
Pre-warm one 24-well plate for each line by placing it inside the 37°C incubator for at least 15 min.
Identify the sample to be thawed and locate the cryovial from the LN2 tank.
Remove the cryovial(s) from the LN2 tank and place on dry ice.
Thaw the cryovial content by incubating it in the water bath at 37°C until a little piece of ice is left (approximately 1–3 min).
Spray the thawed cryovial with 70% ethanol and transfer it to the biosafety cabinet.
Reconstitute thawed cells from the cryovial by adding its content to 9 mL of Advanced DMEM/F12 on ice.
Centrifuge the TO-containing tube at 200 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant carefully, keeping the TO pellet intact.
Resuspend the TO pellet in the required volume (50 μL per well) of Matrigel to achieve a density of 100,000 cells/well.
Mix the TO pellet with Matrigel slowly and without compressing the pipette plunger fully to avoid bubbles.
Pipette 50 μL of the TO-Matrigel mix into the center of each well of the pre-warmed 24-well plate.
Avoid touching the bottom of the well or dispensing to the second stop of the pipette tip to prevent bubbles.
Carefully place the 24-well plate with the TOs in the incubator for 15 min to let the Matrigel polymerize.
Once the Matrigel domes have polymerized, add 500 μL of TO growth media supplemented with 10 μM ROCK inhibitor to each well.
If few wells are plated, add 500 μL of PBS to the wells surrounding those containing TOs to help reduce media evaporation.
Sterilize the hood and equipment before beginning the procedure.
Obtain a single-cell suspension if TOs are healthy, abundant, and no cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are present.
Refer to troubleshooting problem 6 for a strategy to reduce CAFs in culture if they are present visually by brightfield microscopy.
Thaw Matrigel on ice at 4°C.
Maintain Matrigel at 4°C.
Ensure the cell/Matrigel mixture is mixed homogeneously before pipetting the Matrigel dome.
Passage TOs when they reach an appropriate density or if cells begin to die in the middle, adhere to the bottom of the well, or grow out of the Matrigel.
Thaw Matrigel as needed for the experiment.
Warm a 24-well plate in an incubator.
Gently remove media from TOs by pipetting it out or aspirating.
Add 500 μL of TrypLE to each well containing TOs.
Disrupt the TO-containing Matrigel domes by pipetting up and down with TrypLE carefully.
Pipette the TOs into a 15-mL, low-binding centrifuge tube.
Rinse the wells of the 24-well plate with TrypLE to collect remaining TOs and add to the tube.
Place the tube in a 37°C water bath for 10 minutes.
Pipette the supernatant up and down to further break up the TOs.
Spin the cells at 200 g for 5 minutes in a 4°C centrifuge.
Carefully pipette out and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL PBS.
Mix well and count cells using Countess II or an alternate instrument such as a hemocytometer.
Mix equal volumes of cell suspension and trypan blue to assess viability.
Use viable cell numbers to determine plating density.
Centrifuge the cell-containing tube at 200 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Add the requisite volume (50 μL per well) of Matrigel to the single cell/TO pellet to be plated.
Gently pipette the Matrigel up-and-down to incorporate the pelleted cells/TOs until the mixture appears homogeneous.
Remove the pre-warmed plate from the incubator and use a 200 μL pipet, set to a 50 μL volume, to gently pipette the Matrigel/cell mixture up and down to re-homogenize.
Dispense 50 μL of Matrigel/cell mixture in the center of each desired well in the warmed 24-well plate.
Avoid touching the bottom of the plate with the pipette tip to prevent bubbles from forming.
Fill all desired wells following this procedure.
Cover the plate with a lid and return it to the 37°C incubator for at least 15 minutes to allow Matrigel domes to polymerize.
Visually inspect the plate after incubation to ensure that the domes have properly set.
Prepare TO growth media containing ROCK inhibitor at a final concentration of 10 μM while the Matrigel is polymerizing.
Once the domes are fully polymerized, gently pipette 500 μL of pre-warmed (37°C) TO growth media into each well.
Direct the flow of media onto the wall of each well to avoid dispensing it directly on the domes.
Return the plate to a 37°C incubator.
Re-suspend the cell pellet in 1 mL cold TO growth media.
Mix well and count cells using Countess II or an alternate instrument such as a hemocytometer.
Mix equal volumes of cell suspension and trypan blue to assess viability.
Use viable cell numbers to determine plating density.
Note: The following calculations are for plating 2,000 cells per well in all wells of columns 2–23 of a 384-well plate.
Adjust cell numbers and media/Matrigel volumes as needed for alternate plate layouts.
Final volume per well is 20 μL of a 70% media / 30% Matrigel mix with a concentration of 100 cells/μL.
Determine the volume needed for 790,000 cells and transfer cells to a new 15-mL, low-binding centrifuge tube.
Aliquot as many batches of cells as there are drug assays (plates) to set up.
Bring the volume of media to 5,530 μL using ice cold TO growth media.
Keep the 15-mL tubes of cells on ice.
Add 2,370 μL of Matrigel to each cell suspension and mix thoroughly by pipetting.
Plate cells using a liquid handling machine.
Dilute Matrigel to 30% in cold media for repeat dispensing.
Change tips if Matrigel solidifies in pipette tips.
Manually add 20 μL of cell suspension to wells not receiving cells from the Integra.
Pipette 80 μL of PBS to each well of columns 1 and 24.
Add PBS to all wells immediately surrounding those with cells for alternative plate layouts.
Cover the plate with a Breathe-Easy sealing membrane.
Replace the plastic plate cover after applying the sealing membrane.
Move the plate to the incubator.
Locate the appropriate drug aliquots needed for the drug library.
Thaw the drug aliquots at room temperature.
Vortex or heat as necessary to resuspend if particulate matter is observed after thawing.
Put a Bio-Rad Hard shell 96-well plate in the biosafety cabinet and label it with project name, date, expiration date (1 month after preparation), and drug volume.
Pipette the appropriate volume of each drug into the correct well based on the drug library plate map.
Mark the side of the plate with a tally to keep track of freeze-thaw count and expiration date if the drug library is to be used more than once.
Tightly seal an AlumaSeal II on the top of the plate.
Store the drug library at −20°C or −80°C depending on vendor recommendation.
Prepare 13.5 mL of growth media per 384-well assay plate.
Mix the appropriate amount of IncuCyte® Caspase-3/7 Green Apoptosis Assay Reagent with the growth media at a 2× dilution of 2.5 μM (6.75 μL / 13.5 mL).
Aliquot 500 μL of the mixture for 0.1% DMSO vehicle control wells.
Dilute 1.0 μL of DMSO to 500 μL of Caspase-3/7 and media mix for a 0.2% DMSO vehicle control.
Aliquot 500 μL of the mixture for 10 μM staurosporine control wells.
Dilute 1.0 μL of 10 mM staurosporine to 500 μL of Caspase-3/7 and media mix for a 20 μM staurosporine control.
Add 25–30 mL of media/Caspase-3/7 mix to the reservoir (or whatever remains if only one assay plate is used/remains).
Choose and run the Integra program based on the number of assay plates that will have compounds added.
Distribute media for one assay plate into columns 2–9 of the setup plate.
Distribute media for a second assay plate into columns 17–24 of the setup plate.
Pipette 90 μL of media/Caspase-3/7 mix into columns 2–8 and 17–23.
Pipette 98 μL of media/Caspase-3/7 mix into columns 9 and 24.
Pipette 2 μL of 10 mM drug stock into column 9 to generate a 200 μM dilution.
Mix the media/drug mix in column 9 up-and-down ten times.
Transfer 10 μL from column 9 to column 8 to generate a 10-fold dilution.
Repeat mixing and transferring steps for columns 7 through 1, creating serial dilutions.
If necessary, repeat pipetting and serial dilution process for columns 17–24.
Distribute 50 μL of control mixes into columns 1 and 16.
Mix 0.2% DMSO and 20 μl staurosporine controls every other row in rows A-H.
Transfer 20 μl of controls and each drug dilution to the appropriate well in the 384-well cell plate using an Integra Assist Plus program or by hand.
Pre-warm an aliquot of Advanced DMEM/F-12 to room temperature.
Determine how much media is needed based on how many wells of the 384-well drug assay plate are to be treated.
Add Hoechst 33342 and TO-PRO-3 to each aliquot of media.
Use 7 μl of 1 mM stock of TO-PRO-3 for standard 384-well layout with 7,740 μL media.
Use 5.8 μl of 10 mg/mL stock of Hoechst 33342 for the same layout and volume.
Dispense the total volume of fluorescent dye-containing media to a reservoir.
Distribute 20 μL from the reservoir to each well using The Integra Assist Plus Pipetting Robot or by hand using a multi-channel pipette.
Return plate to incubator for 2 h before imaging.
Design an acquisition protocol suitable for imaging targets of interest (TOs) in 3-dimensional space.
Include a Z-series that will encompass most TOs without excessively increasing imaging time.
Set exposure times for each individual fluorophore to maximize signal-to-noise ratio without saturating the signal.
Image multiple sites per well to ensure enough TOs are imaged for analysis.
Use a 10× objective for resolution and throughput.
Test the acquisition settings in multiple wells.
Save the acquisition settings to be used for all plates.
Run the acquisition protocol on all plates immediately after dye addition.
Ensure that the imaging occurs exactly 2 hours post-dye addition.
Discard completed plates by sealing them properly.
Dispose of sealed plates in biohazard waste containers designated for chemotherapy or other hazardous compounds.
